{{Quote|Perhaps you would like to learn something before you die. The use of two blades, one to support the other, can be traced back thousands of years and was common to both of our species. The invention of lightsabers has done nothing to lessen the effectiveness of this strategy&mdash;as you are about to learn.|[[Boc Aseca]] to [[Kyle Katarn]]|<ref name="Dark Forces: Jedi Knight">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref>}}
'''Jar'Kai''' was originally a style of swordplay that utilized dual weapons, developed by the [[Yovshin Swordsmen]]. A similar dual-blade technique referred to as '''Niman''' was developed by the [[Royale Machetero]]s of the [[Kashi Mer Dynasty|Kashi Mer]] monarchy. [[Form VI/Legends|Niman]] was adopted by the [[darksider]] group known as the [[Legions of Lettow]] during the [[First Great Schism]], as well as the Jedi Order itself. Niman was developed into the sixth form of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|Lightsaber combat]], retaining its name.<ref name="TCSWE" />

It should be noted that the fourth form of lightsaber combat, [[Form IV/Legends|Ataru]], was also known to employ dual blades as part of its training regimen. [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] was a master in this form when she was only a Padawan, an accomplishment that Jedi Masters would have serious troubles in achieving.<ref name="TCSWE" /><ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref><ref name="FJLC">{{InsiderCite|62|Fightsaber: Jedi Lightsaber Combat}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|This challenge you will not overcome. Your lightsaber is nothing against the power of the dark side.''"<br />"''That's why I always carry two.|An unknown Sith and Fortris Gall|<ref name="Threat Peace 2">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 2: New Galactic Order]]''</ref>}}
[[File:ExarKunTraining-DLOTS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], a Niman practitioner, taking up a second blade in training.]]
The Jar'Kai style developed by the Yovshin Swordsmen was named for a [[Jar'Kai (city)|city]] on [[Atrisia/Legends|Atrisia]]. The city of Jar'Kai was also the site where the original [[Jar'Kai dueling saber]]s were crafted. These weapons were utilized by the Yovshin and were designed for the express purpose of being dual-wielded.<ref name="dfs4" />

[[Form VI/Legends|Niman]], the dual-blade style developed by the Royale Macheteros of the Kashi Mer, was named for the dual triumvirate of the Kashi deities. The style was adopted by the Legions of Lettow,<ref name="dfs4" /> a group of [[Darksider]]s responsible for the First Great Schism of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. After the defeat of the Legion at the hands of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], Niman was adopted by the Jedi Order, eventually being refined into the sixth form of lightsaber combat, referred to by the same name.<ref name="TCSWE" /> It should be noted that there were Jedi who engaged in dual-blade combat prior to the adoption of Niman by the Order, an example being [[Awdrysta Pina]], who wielded a pair of [[Force-imbued sword/Legends|Jedi katanas]] in battle.<ref name="dfs4" /> Many [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] and [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] trained to use Form VI in the hopes of gaining a basic knowledge of the dual-bladed combat, but very few ever achieved complete mastery of Niman.

Dual-blade practitioners of Niman included [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kavar]], who utilized a [[Shoto lightsaber/Legends|shoto]] as his secondary weapon, and the Jedi trainee turned [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Lord [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], who took up an additional weapon on occasion. However there were few dual-blade duelists that practiced classic Niman, though the Jar'Kai tactic saw fervent usage. Numerous Jedi and Sith were known to take up a secondary blade in combat, though few did so regularly.

==Description==
[[File:VentresReusDuel2-TVO.png|thumb|right|200px|Asajj Ventress engaging Jedi Master Keelyvine Reus in combat]]
Dual-blade fighters, whether classical Niman duelists or individuals applying the Jar'Kai tactic, were able to maintain a strong offense, as the speed of attack that two blades allowed would overwhelm most opponents. A typical maneuver was to continually attack with one blade while relying on the other for defensive coverage, ensuring that the duelist could keep up his guard even as he attacked. However, it was common that both blades were used for offensive purposes, keeping up a continuous wave-front assault.

Another advantage of Jar'Kai was that the two blades made it easier to hold off multiple opponents, as one simply had more blades to parry with. [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], a dual-blade practitioner, demonstrated this during her [[Mission to Ruul (Clone Wars)|mission on Ruul]], where she held her own against up to three Jedi simultaneously.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu">''[[Jedi: Mace Windu]]''</ref> Dual blades could also be used as a defensive or compensatory measure when engaging another opponent who utilized multiple blades in combat,<ref name="Return">{{TORweb|url=info/media/trailers/return|text="Return"|int=Return (cinematic trailer)}}</ref> as shown when Kit Fisto stole and took up one of the blades of the cyborg [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], whose mechanical anatomy allowed him to wield up to four [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] at once.<ref name="LOG">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}}</ref>

Known Jar'Kai techniques and maneuvers include the "Rising Whirlwind", which consisted of a duelist swinging his blades about his body, creating a "whirlwind" of deadly attacks, and the "Twin Strike", in which both blades were swung in an arc towards the opponent in a deadly power attack.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

Though a complete fighting system in and of itself, Jar'Kai was easily adapted to other styles. After beginning her tutelage under [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]], Asajj Ventress quickly applied [[Form II/Legends|Makashi]] techniques to her practice of Jar'Kai. As Makashi was Tyranus's favored form, Jedi Master [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] was able to recognize his training techniques in Asajj's fighting abilities, stating as much. [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] also infused Jar'Kai tactics into his own [[Form VII/Legends|Vaapad]] style while on a mission on [[Haruun Kal/Legends|Haruun Kal]], his former apprentice, [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]], doing likewise.

===Weaknesses===
{{Quote|&hellip;such fighters tended to rely too much on their blades, and pay too little attention to the Force.|[[Jai Maruk]]'s thoughts on Jar'Kai|<ref name="YDR">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref>}}
[[File:VentressVsSkywalkerRain-Chapter19.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Anakin Skywalker battering away Asajj Ventress' defense with a series of power strokes, demonstrating one of the primary weaknesses of Jar'Kai.]]
Despite the advantages offered, Jar'Kai was not without its drawbacks. Firstly, as both hands held individual lightsabers, two-handed blows were impossible, and the duelist was unable to put all his or her weight behind blocks, weakening the defensive capabilities. Thus, an enemy with a single hilt could simply assault a Jar'Kai practitioners defense with brute force, battering away until the dual-blade duelist's guard gave way, as shown during [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] duel with Asajj Ventress on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. However, this weakness was hardly absolute, as some duelists possessed the physical strength to block power attacks with only one arm, examples including Grievous, whose mechanically augmented strength allowed him to both effectively defend against and dole out heavy power blows.<ref name="LoE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> Asajj Ventress eventually developed the physical strength necessary to compensate for this weakness, being able to hold up simultaneous bladelocks with both Anakin Skywalker and [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], both of whom were [[Form V/Legends|Form V]] practitioners;<ref name="CWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> she had even withstood two separate bladelocks with the towering General Grievous, who was using all four of his lightsabers.<ref name="Massacre">{{TCW|Massacre}}</ref>

Secondly, because of the gyroscopic effect inherent in lightsabers, dual blades were more difficult to control than a single blade. Due to this, special training was required to practice Jar'Kai, and without it, a secondary blade was more often a hindrance than an advantage. Fortunately, dual-blade training was often quite standard amongst most [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-using organizations, though advanced training seemed somewhat rarer.<ref name="FJLC" /><ref name="JVS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

A third trait worthy of note is that Jar'Kai practitioners were often overly reliant on their weapons and bladework, leaving their abilities in other areas undeveloped.<ref name="YDR" /> An example of this weakness was evident in the Jedi Battlemaster [[Raskta Lsu]], who was an exceptional duelist, but in her devotion to lightsaber combat, she never developed her abilities in the Force, forcing her to rely on both her skill with the blade(s) and the support of more Force-adept allies to compensate.<ref name="DBROT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> Some duelists, such as Asajj Ventress, would become overly reliant on simply having two blades to back up one another, and would be left at a disadvantage if deprived of the one;<ref name="TCWF">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref> however, this weakness could be overcome with time.<ref name="TCW 9">[[The Clone Wars 9|''The Clone Wars'' 9]]</ref>

[[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], while facing the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Komari Vosa]] on [[Cog Hive Seven]], saw Jar'Kai as "predictable." This would make sense,<ref name="Lockdown">''[[Maul: Lockdown]]''</ref> given that his [[Sith Master/Legends|mentor]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], could wield two sabers at any time.<ref name="The Lawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref><ref name="Shadow Conspiracy">''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]''</ref>

===Weapon Specifications===
{{Quote|Those who wish to incorporate a second blade may wish to use a lightsaber shoto in their off-hand, for its shorter blade allows for a greater range of motion.|[[Skarch Vaunk]] on dual-blade combat in ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]''|<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>}}
As both Niman and Jar'Kai were developed prior to the invention of lightsabers, they were designed with metal blades in mind. Jar'Kai even had a type of sword created that was specialized to the use of the dual-blade style, the Jar'Kai dueling saber. However, due to the sword-like nature of lightsabers, the styles were relatively easily adapted.

[[File:Brood_vs_Starkiller.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Maris Brood]] wielding a set of [[Guard shoto/Legends|Guard shotos]] against [[Galen Marek]].]]
Traditional Niman dual-blade regiments were based around wielding a short lightsaber, the Shoto, as the off-hand weapon, as the smaller blade was easier to control.<ref name="TJP" /> This seemed to be a relatively common practice amongst Jar'Kai duelists within the Jedi Order, with such individuals such as [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]],<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /> [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]],<ref name="SWBF2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> and others doing so. The Zabrak [[Maris Brood]] even took this idea a step further and wielded dual [[Guard shoto/Legends|guard shotos]] in combat.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

However, since such specialized weapons were not required to utilize Jar'Kai, many dual-blade combatants simply wielded two standard blades in combat. In fact, weapons other than lightsabers have even been wielded as secondaries, examples including [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaffs]], as demonstrated by [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]]<ref name="CWC25">{{CW|25}}</ref> and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]],<ref name="Grievous Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref> swords composed of a lightsaber-resistant material, which [[Revan/Legends|Revan]]<ref name="Kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> or [[Meetra Surik]]<ref name="Kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> conceivably did, or even simple knives, as shown by [[Mara Jade Skywalker]].<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> Obi-Wan Kenobi even used a [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] on one occasion.<ref name="TCD">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref> Also, the number of lightsabers wielded was not limited to two, depending on the duelist's anatomy. Among the Jedi, [[Priapulin]] Master [[Skwelli]] was renowned for wielding six lightsabers.<ref name="TJP" /> General Grievous would often wield four, splitting his mechanical arms to produce an extra set of appendages.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Thanks to [[Repulsorlift/Legends|Repulsorlifts]] built into his legs, Grievous was capable of wielding six sabers, grasping them in his talon-like feet, though he has never been recorded doing so.<ref name="LoE" /> The [[Besalisk/Legends|Besalisk]] Jedi [[Pong Krell/Legends|Pong Krell]] would also take advantage of his extra set of arms to dual-wield [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|double-bladed lightsabers]].<ref name="DarknessOnUmbara">{{TCW|Darkness on Umbara}}</ref>

==Applications==
{{Quote|I am working on this, mostly as an exercise in control. I doubt I will ever need to use it.|Anakin Skywalker comments on studying dual-blade combat in his copy of ''The Jedi Path''|<ref name="TJP" />}}
[[File:SkywalkerJarKaiAtaru.jpg|thumb|left|Anakin Skywalker applies dual-blade combat against Dooku.]]
Anakin Skywalker applied Jar'Kai in battle, in conjunction with his skills in [[Form IV/Legends|Ataru]], during his duel with Count Dooku on Geonosis. While his sudden flurry of attack momentarily caught Dooku off guard, Skywalker's lack of advanced training in either Jar'Kai or Ataru allowed Dooku to break through the Jedi's array of weapons, forcing Skywalker onto the defensive before destroying one of the lightsabers.<ref name="FJLC" /> Skywalker's master, Obi-Wan Kenobi, also displayed skill in dual-blade combat, taking up the lightsaber of deceased Jedi [[Ky Narec/Legends|Ky Narec]], alongside his own during his duel with Narec's fallen student, Asajj Ventress, on [[Rattatak/Legends|Rattatak]].<ref name="HAF">[[Republic 60|''Republic'' 60]]</ref> Skywalker himself applied Jar'Kai in battle several more times during the Clone Wars, such as during a battle with fallen Jedi [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]] in the aftermath of the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar/Legends|bombing of the Jedi Temple]].<ref name="The Wrong Jedi">{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}}</ref>

Ventress, herself a Jar'Kai practitioner, originally took up the style after Narec's death, wielding his lightsaber alongside her own. However, without Narec's guidance, she spiraled down the path of the dark side, and this showed in her bladework, which became furiously aggressive. She demonstrated her skills to Count Dooku during his visit to Rattatak, viciously killing off the competitors in [[The Cauldron]] in a furious display of bladework and raw power in the Force. During her subsequent duel with the Count, she fell on him in a blind fury, but was nonetheless defeated. However, she did impress the Count and his Sith Master, Darth Sidious, with her skills. The Count awarded her with a high-ranking position within the CIS military, and the twin curved lightsabers of his former student, Komari Vosa.<ref name="CWC7">{{CW|7}}</ref> Wielding these new lightsabers, Ventress developed her skills under Dooku's tutelage, applying her skills in dual-blade combat to Makashi.<ref name="COD">{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}}</ref> Eventually, her prowess as a duelist allowed her to hold her own against up to three adversaries with little difficulty, as she demonstrated during her mission to [[Ruul (moon)|Ruul]].<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" />

[[File:Duel_on_Kinooine.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Luke Skywalker utilizing dual-blades.]]
Her skills even advanced to the point where she was able to battle and defeat or at least hold her own against Jedi Council masters, something few of her contemporaries could do.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /><ref name="TCD" /> However, despite her skills, she was not without her weaknesses. During her earlier years, she lacked the major levels of physical strength to compensate for the inherent weaknesses of Jar'Kai; her blows lacked power, as shown by Dooku's casual defensive moves during their bout on Rattatak;<ref name="CWC7" /> and she was left vulnerable to power attacks, as shown by her retreat before Anakin Skywalker's offensive frenzy during their duel on Yavin IV.<ref name="CWC19">{{CW|19}}</ref> However, she eventually developed the physical strength necessary to compensate for this weakness, demonstrating the ability to hold up simultaneous bladelocks with both Anakin Skywalker and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], Ahsoka Tano,<ref name="TCWF" /> both of whom were Form V practitioners.<ref name="CWCG" />

It is also known that Darth Maul trained in Jar'Kai and had mastered it enough that even Darth Plagueis acknowledged Maul's skill in dual-blade combat.<ref name="Resurrection">{{Tales|9|Resurrection (comic story)}}</ref><ref name="Darth P">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> However, Maul rarely used Jar'Kai and preferred to wield a saberstaff instead, as shown during his duels with Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> During much of the Clone Wars, he also seemed to favor more of a single-blade approach than dual-wielding, as seen in his duels with Obi-Wan Kenobi. However, he had managed to defend against and defeat Komari Vosa, even if she had a two-to-one saber advantage over him.<ref name="Lockdown" /> In his final duel on Mandalore with Darth Sidious, Maul took up both his own saber and the [[Darksaber/Legends|Darksaber]]. Despite rarely using it, his skill in Jar'Kai had clearly greatly improved, managing to fight almost evenly with his former master, who also used dual blades, although he was ultimately overpowered.<ref name="The Lawless" /> When the reborn Maul [[Duel on Kalakar Six|dueled]] with Darth Vader on [[Kalakar Six]], he employed Jar'Kai after his saberstaff been [[Sun djem/Legends|sliced in half]], enabling him to cut loose and bring Vader to his knees.<ref name="Resurrection" />

Luke Skywalker initially took to wielding dual-blades to combat [[Lumiya]]'s [[Lumiya's lightwhip|lightwhip]], as the multiple extensions of the elaborate weapon made short work of a standard defensive technique. In their rematch, Skywalker used his newly fabricated shoto to back up [[Luke Skywalker's green lightsaber/Legends|his full-length lightsaber]], entangling the energy beams of her whip with one blade while cutting apart the physical strands. Skywalker managed to disarm Lumiya by shorting out the energy beam of her whip with a power attack, though he lost his lightsaber in the process, before he attacked her with the shoto.<ref name="SW96:DWaDL">[[Star Wars (1977) 96|''Star Wars'' (1977) 96]]</ref> Dual-blade combat became one of Skywalker's preferred methods for dealing with lightwhips, and he utilized it several times during various rematches with Lumiya, though in their last engagement, he fought her only with a single weapon. He also encouraged his wife, Mara Jade Skywalker, to construct a shoto of her own for the same reasons.<ref name="Sacrifice" /><ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref> Skywalker would also display his skills with dual blades while training his students.<ref name="CE3:EmpireLost1">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 1|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 1]]</ref>

==Practitioners==
{{Quote|It strikes me as unnecessary, but I won't deny his mastery of the Jar'Kai technique.|Darth Plagueis comments on Darth Maul's combat ability|<ref name="Darth P" />}}
[[File:Kyle_boc.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Dark Jedi [[Boc Aseca]] utilizing Jar'Kai against [[Kyle Katarn]].]]
While many duelists have utilized Jar'Kai at some point, fewer combatants did so on a regular basis. Among the ancient Jedi who did so are [[Awdrysta Pina]], who practiced with a pair of Jedi katanas, Kavar,<ref name="Kotor" /> [[Bastila Shan]], [[Vandar Tokare]]<ref name="KotOR CG" /> and [[Fortris Gall]].<ref name="Threat Peace 2" />

During the [[Jedi Civil War]], many of the Dark Jedi that pledged their allegiance to [[Darth/Legends|Darths]] Revan and [[Darth Malak|Malak's]] [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] used Jar'Kai against their former Jedi brethren.<ref name="Kotor" /> Many of the Sith following [[Kreia|Darth Traya's]] [[Sith Triumvirate]] applied the Jar'Kai form in combat.<ref name="Kotor2" />

During the [[New Sith Wars]], the Sith Lord known as the [[Dark Underlord]] practiced Jar'Kai, wielding two [[Sith sword]]s. During this time, the style also had its share of Jedi practitioners, including the [[Echani/Legends|Echani]] Jedi Master [[Raskta Lsu]],<ref name="DBROT" /> and the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] Jedi [[Newar Forrth]]. Over a millennium later, the Twi'lek Dark Jedi [[Boc Aseca]] attempted to imitate Forrth, resulting in a clumsy, though effective fighting method.<ref name="Star wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], General Grievous included elements of Jar'Kai in his style of combat. He commonly utilized two lightsabers in battle, but demonstrated the ability to wield four lightsabers, achieving this by splitting his mechanical arms and hands along their lengths, resulting in four arms.<ref name="ROTS" /> Grievous' contemporaries, Asajj Ventress, [[Sora Bulq/Legends|Sora Bulq]] and [[Saato]] also utilized Jar'Kai in combat.<ref name="CWC7" /><ref name="TNDA">''[[Star Wars: The New Droid Army]]''</ref> Bulq himself, a master of all known forms of lightsaber combat, often wielded a shoto in combat as his secondary weapon, applying his skills in Jar'Kai to his practice of Vaapad, the legendary Form VII variant that he had aided Mace Windu in developing prior to his defection to the CIS.<ref name="Jedi: Mace Windu" /> Other Jar'Kai practitioners active during the Clone Wars included Jedi [[Keelyvine Reus]] and [[Pong Krell/Legends|Pong Krell]]. Darth Sidious also was extremely skilled in Niman/Jar'Kai, utilizing both his primary and backup lightsabers to fight his former Sith apprentice Darth Maul and [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], although he rarely used it, his skill allowed him to prevail against their combined abilities and overpower Maul using the same shortly after his brother's death.<ref name="The Lawless" /><ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" />

[[File:AhsokaLightsabers-Overlords.png|thumb|right|180px|Ahsoka wielding her green lightsaber and yellow-green shoto]]
Ahsoka Tano was also skilled in the use of Jar'Kai and wielded both a lightsaber and a shoto. She employed an extremely complicated Ataru-Shien reverse grip style to her Jar'Kai tactic that was worthy of mastery. She was able to hold her own against both Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi on Mortis and provide a challenge for Grievous, who was himself a master of Jar'Kai and was using four lightsabers at the time. Tano lasted far longer against Grievous than she had in their previous duel on Skytop Station, which happened before she started using two lightsabers. Tano later lost her shoto and it was shown that she had become somewhat vulnerable to the weakness of getting too reliant on it, a trait she shared with Asajj Ventress, and when using a single lightsaber, she was unable to defeat the treacherous Barriss Offee in combat.<ref name="Altar of Mortis">{{TCW|Altar of Mortis (episode)}}</ref><ref name="A Necessary Bond">{{TCW|A Necessary Bond}}</ref><ref name="The Jedi Who Knew Too Much">{{TCW|The Jedi Who Knew Too Much}}</ref><ref name="To Catch a Jedi">{{TCW|To Catch a Jedi}}</ref>

It should be noted that Count Dooku, a famed Makashi practitioner, considered dual-blade combat styles inferior, believing that duelists should either make do with a single blade or not at all. He even went so far as to fault double-bladed lightsabers for this.<ref name="LoE" />

During the Dark Times, a notable Jar'Kai practitioner was the Zabrak Jedi Padawan Maris Brood, who used two [[Guard shoto/Legends|guard shotos]] in combat against Darth Vader's secret apprentice, [[Galen Marek]].<ref name="TFU" /> Many of [[Aberrant clone|Marek's unstable clones]]&mdash;including the two more successful clones, [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]] and the [[Dark Apprentice]]&mdash;adopted the form during their training under Vader, utilizing it during their emergence.<ref name="TFU2">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref> Starkiller studied Ataru and Niman to take advantage of their dual-blade training regimes and facilitate his mastery of Jar'Kai, also frequently chaining in Force-based attacks as part of Niman into his bladework.<ref name="TFU2n">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> Two of Darth Sidious's Dark Jedi, [[Jeng Droga]]<ref name="The Dark Forces Saga">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050407a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 1}}</ref> and [[Sa Cuis]]<ref name="In His Image">{{StoryCite|story=In His Image|book=Vader: The Ultimate Guide}}</ref> favored dual-blades.
[[File:TwinStrike-TPOV.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Dark Jedi Jar'Kai practitioner]]
[[10 ABY/Legends|Fourteen years]] after the destruction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]], many of [[New Reborn]] were trained to use the Jar'Kai style, most notably Axmis' apprentice, [[Alora (Dark Jedi)|Alora]]. Many Jedi also used Jar'Kai to combat Axmis' Reborn.<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

Clone Wars-era Jedi Knight [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]] was a known dual-blade fighter, using his [[Sharad Hett|late father's]] weapon alongside with his own.<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Emissaries to Malastare">''[[Star Wars: Emissaries to Malastare]]''</ref> After he fell to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and became the Sith Lord Darth Krayt, he continued to practice Jar'Kai in conjunction with his knowledge of Form VI lightsaber combat.<ref name="Legacy 1">[[Legacy (2006) 1|''Legacy'' (2006) 1]]</ref><ref name="LECG">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Various members of [[One Sith|Krayt's Sith Order]] also practiced Jar'Kai, including the [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|third Darth Wyyrlok]]<ref name="Legacy 2006 14">[[Legacy (2006) 14|''Legacy'' (2006) 14]]</ref><ref name="Legacy 2006 27">[[Legacy (2006) 27|''Legacy'' (2006) 27]], Cover only</ref> and [[Darth Reave]].<ref name="Legacy 2006 29">[[Legacy (2006) 29|''Legacy'' (2006) 29]]</ref>

Other Jar'Kai practitioners included the Jedi [[Micah Giiett]],<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Council: Acts of War">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Council: Acts of War]]''</ref> [[Joclad Danva/Legends|Joclad Danva]],<ref name="Medstar1">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref> and [[Serra Keto]].<ref name="ROTS video game">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref>

===Alternative Uses===
{{Quote|Two blades&mdash;one long and one short?''"<br />"''Against the two natures of your weapon.|Luke Skywalker, explains the use of dual-blades to Lumiya just prior to their duel|<ref name="SW96:DWaDL" />}}
Some duelists maintain skill in dual-blade combat, and utilize it often, but not on a regular basis.

In the [[1000 BBY/Legends|final year]] of the New Sith Wars, before the events of the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], the Sith Lord and [[Sith Blademaster]] [[Kas'im]] displayed his skills in dual-blade combat against against [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], utilizing the Ataru subform. Kas'im, who had mastered all of the seven classic forms and normally used a double-bladed lightsaber, always discouraged his students at the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Korriban Sith Academy]] against using Jar'Kai, claiming that it was inherently flawed. However, Kas'im's expertise with Jar'Kai was such that he was able to confuse Bane and nearly defeat him.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" />

[[File:Weapon_Mastery_TCG_by_Baracchi.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Jedi using Jar'Kai against [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].]]
Jedi duelists known to apply Jar'Kai on occasion include [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], who wielded a shoto alongside her lightsaber during many of the more chaotic battles of the Clone Wars,<ref name="SWBF2" /> though she was perfectly able utilizing a regular blade as her secondary weapon.<ref name="HoF">{{StoryCite|story=Heart of Fire (comic story)|book=Dark Horse Extra|bformatted=''Dark Horse Extra'' 35&ndash;37}}</ref>

The [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] of the [[New Jedi Order]] Luke Skywalker displayed his skill with the dual-bladed tactic during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], often utilizing it with a shoto in conjunction with his regular lightsaber. Approximately five years after the end of the [[Swarm War]], Skywalker applied Jar'Kai in actual combat against the Dark Lady Lumiya on [[Roqoo Depot]]<ref name="Tempest" /> and at [[Gilatter VIII]] during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Exile">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref> Luke Skywalker's wife Mara Jade built a shoto per his request when Lumiya re-emerged. She was with Luke on Roqoo Depot when he fought Lumiya; at the same time she dueled Dark Jedi [[Alema Rar]].<ref name="Tempest" /> Mara Jade also used a variant of Jar'Kai when she [[Skirmish on Kavan|dueled]] her nephew and Lumiya's Sith apprentice [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] on the planet [[Kavan]], using her shoto and vibroblade.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

The Sith Master [[Lomi Plo]] used Jar'Kai against Skywalker twice out of the three times they dueled, using a standard lightsaber and a shoto.<ref name="Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen">''[[Dark Nest II: The Unseen Queen]]''</ref><ref name="Dark Nest III: The Swarm War">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref>

===Situational Applications===
{{Quote|What was to become of elegance and gallantry if a duelist couldn't make do with one blade?|[[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] thoughts on Jar'Kai|<ref name="LoE" />}}
[[File:Malgus-Return.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Darth Malgus wielding dual-blades.]]
During the [[Battle of Korriban]] during the [[Great Galactic War]], Jedi Master [[Kao Cen Darach]] wielded his own single-bladed and his apprentice's double-bladed lightsabers against [[Darth Vindican|Vindican]] and his apprentice, [[Darth Malgus|Malgus]]. While Darach injured Vindican, Malgus followed the Jedi's example and took up his own master's lightsaber, using the extra blade to counter Darach's array of weapons and cut him down.<ref name="Return" />

Kit Fisto took up the lightsaber of his former Padawan, [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]], during his duel with General Grievous, in order to even the odds against the General's multiple weapons. Using the lightsaber, he unleashed his own skill with Jar'Kai, utilizing it in conjunction with his mastery of [[Form I/Legends|Form I]] lightsaber combat, driving back Grievous and holding his own against three of the General's [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]].<ref name="LOG" />

In addition to his use of the fighting method against Dooku on Geonosis, Anakin Skywalker performed Jar'Kai against [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]], using his own lightsaber and that of his Padawan, Ahsoka Tano, in the [[Devaron system/Legends|Devaron system]], and in the [[Progate Temple/Legends|Progate Temple]] on Geonosis, using [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli's]] lightsaber before releasing her from [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Karina the Great/Legends|Karina the Great]] and returning it to her. He also used Jar'Kai against former Knight Barriss Offee.<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" />

[[File:LukeVersusShimrra.jpg|thumb|right|Luke Skywalker utilizing Jar'Kai against [[Shimrra Jamaane]].]]
During their participation in the [[Summertime War]] on Haruun Kal, Mace Windu and his former student, Depa Billaba, both applied their mastery of Form VII lightsaber combat with dual blades on occasion.<ref name="SPn">[[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']]</ref> Shaak Ti also appeared to have some training in the style, as she expertly wielded an electrostaff in conjunction with her lightsaber during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]];<ref name="CWC25" /> sources describe her wielding dual lightsabers after the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Jedi Purge]].

Former Jedi Barriss Offee also displayed considerable prowess in Jar'Kai having stolen Asajj Ventress' lightsabers. Her skill was great enough to overwhelm Ahsoka Tano and hold her own very well against Anakin Skywalker.<ref name="To Catch a Jedi" /><ref name="The Wrong Jedi" />

It is known that many, if not all, duelists have applied Jar'Kai in combat at some point, even if they lacked specialist knowledge, usually doing so whenever the situation demanded and/or facilitated it. Duelists known to do so include [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]],<ref name="TSW">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War]]''</ref> [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]],<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: The Hunt for Aurra Sing">''[[Star Wars: The Hunt for Aurra Sing]]''</ref> [[Lycan]],<ref name="Nomad">{{Tales|issue1=21|issue2=24|Nomad}}</ref> [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]],<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Rite of Passage">''[[Star Wars: Rite of Passage]]''</ref> [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]], [[Anakin Solo]],<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin]]''</ref> [[Saba Sebatyne]],<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Fury">''[[Legacy of the Force: Fury]]''</ref> [[Vestara Khai]],<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Omen">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref> and [[Kol Skywalker]].<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Due to George Lucas' original conception that lightsabers were extremely heavy and difficult to handle, the idea of dual-blade combat was accordingly rendered impossible. However, Lucas eventually decided to make lightsabers lighter to facilitate the faster choreography in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], consequently inferring the possibility of dual-blade fencing.<ref name="BirthOfTheLightsaber">{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars Trilogy (DVD)|featurette=The Birth of the Lightsaber}}</ref> Dual-blade combat made its first appearance in [[Star Wars (1977) 96|''Star Wars'' (1977) 96]], which depicted Luke Skywalker fighting with a short lightsaber as an off-hand weapon to counter Lumiya's use of the lightwhip.

[[William C. Dietz]] and [[Dave Dorman]]'s novella ''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]'', suggests the dual-blade combat predates the invention of the lightsaber. Furthermore, in the ''Star Wars'' computer game ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]'', there is a pair of "Jar'Kai dueling sabers" that are ordinary metal swords. This also suggests that Jar'Kai predated lightsabers, even though the release of ''X-Wing Alliance'' was before the behind the scenes "invention" of lightsaber forms. This was confirmed by a ''[[Wizards of the Coast]]'' supplement, which revealed that the Jar'Kai style, and swords, originated with the Yovshin Swordsmen of Atrisia.

[[File:Dooku2sabers.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Dooku wielding two lightsabers.]]
Originally, Dooku was planned to display ability with two blades against Jedi Master Yoda in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], which would have made him a possible Jar'Kai practitioner. However, the idea was later dropped, and in the novel ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'', Dooku was stated to dislike usages of multiple blades, which made him no longer likely to be a Jar'Kai practitioner. Photos with [[Christopher Lee]] wielding two lightsabers with visual effects became promotional pictures; one of them can be seen in the ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''. Also, the scene where Dooku is wielding two lightsabers was seen in the comic version of ''Attack of the Clones''.

In the video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', a character's skill in the Jar'Kai form was measured by a set of three feats called ''Two-Weapon Fighting''. Acquiring these feats made the character excel in dual sword or lightsaber combat, but it also increased the character's proficiency in wielding double-bladed lightsabers and swords, and even dual [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]].<ref name="Kotor" /> However, in the game's sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', one of the available implants, called the ''Enhancement D-Package'', allowed a character to use two weapons effectively without having to purchase the ''Two-Weapon Fighting'' set of feats.<ref name="Kotor2" /> Furthermore, [[Sith Marauder]]s and [[Jedi Weapon Master]]s had the opportunity of learning the "Superior Two-Weapon Fighting" feats, enabling unparalleled mastery of two-weapon combat.

Similarly, in the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'': [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook|Saga Edition]] characters can take Dual Weapon Mastery feats which serve the same function; oddly enough, none of these feats are required to take the Jar'Kai talent of the Jedi Knight prestige class, although Niman is a prerequisite.
